Baseline 34 Rust tests not regressed. The implementer summary's '79'/'80' is a stale bookkeeping count; the measured tree is 81 with 0 failures. `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -D warnings` are clean (codex, kimi, minimax, glm).

All four lenses ran `cargo run -q -p voicekit-cli -- demo --fake` to exit 0 with providers `stt=fake-stt llm=fake-llm tts=fake-tts vad=fake-vad` and the summary carrying `dropped_frames`, `dropped_ms`, `dropped_events`, and `sidecar_dropped_frames`. Covers tombstone capacity, deterministic oldest-first eviction, the monotonic eviction counter, repeated late `audio_end` no-op for a live tombstone, evicted-id rejection, and post-cancel audio not rebuffered. Kimi and minimax also confirm 27 passed with `PYTHONPATH` unset via the new `sdks/python/tests/conftest.py`.

All four lenses ran `cargo run -q -p voicekit-cli -- demo --sidecar` to exit 0. After revision 2 the demo serves all three adapters from the real Python plugin: `providers stt=sidecar-stt llm=sidecar-llm tts=python-fake vad=fake-vad` (was `stt=fake-stt` in round 1). The summary and TurnDone carry `sidecar_dropped_frames` distinct from the Rust playout `dropped_frames`; the child is reaped via the awaited `client.shutdown()` (`kill_on_drop(true)` bounds the panic path).

All three grep legs exit 0 for all four lenses. Leg 1 finds `sidecar_dropped_frames` on all three provider traits, all three sidecar adapters, the runtime (`events.rs:32`, `session.rs:72`) and the CLI, plus `proptest` in `crates/voicekit-runtime/tests/properties.rs`. Leg 2 finds `MAX_CANCELLED = 256` and the monotonic `evicted` counter in `sdks/python/voicekit_sdk/plugin.py`. Leg 3 (negated `cancelled.add(`) finds no raw insert; every insert goes through `CancelledTombstones.remember` at `plugin.py:274`.

modern_technique_gaps.gap: The `EventQueue` property suite asserts local invariants only; there is no reference-state/model comparison and no one-to-one mapping from ADR invariants to named properties. `take_preserves_survivor_order` is a subsequence check, so a queue that admitted an event it should have refused could still pass.
modern_technique_gaps.suggested_remedy: Advisory (non-blocking): add a model-based property (reference transition function compared against SUT state) or map each ADR invariant to a named property so a spec change cannot silently orphan a test.

modern_technique_gaps.gap: No mutation-testing evidence. `tier3-evidence.log` records 'no mutation tooling configured - skipping', so the property suite is shown to pass but not shown to kill mutants of the accounting/capacity logic.
modern_technique_gaps.suggested_remedy: Advisory (non-blocking): run a mutation tool against `events.rs` (or a deliberately broken `EventQueue` mutant) to demonstrate the properties fail as intended; the accounting property at `properties.rs:97-138` is the natural target.

modern_technique_gaps.gap: Capacities are static and there is no credit/admission-control or occupancy-driven backpressure. TokenFlow-style occupancy-aware scheduling and flow-controlled admission (arXiv:2510.02758, arXiv:2604.11001) are the frontier; Voicekit uses fixed compile-time capacities and drops rather than throttling.
modern_technique_gaps.suggested_remedy: Explicitly out of scope for v0.1 and already stated in the ADR (`docs/adr/0001-architecture.md:43-50`). No action unless a later version targets adaptive/credit backpressure.

low_confidence_claims.claim: A persisted proptest regression seed exists (`properties.proptest-regressions:7`, `capacity = 2, policy = DropOldest, kinds = [Droppable, Droppable]`) proving the accounting property once failed. Minimax asserts it exists; codex reports no such file anywhere; kimi reports revision 2 deleted it. Direct tree inspection by the synthesizer confirms no regressions file is present (`crates/voicekit-runtime/tests/` contains only `properties.rs`), so minimax's citation is stale. Non-load-bearing: the property passes at 128 and 512 cases.

`cargo test --workspace` is not safe in a Python-free environment: two pre-existing sidecar integration tests (`cancel_ends_the_stream_without_killing_the_process`, `supervisor_restarts_a_dead_plugin`) fail with `VOICEKIT_PYTHON=/nonexistent`, unchanged from HEAD. The hard rule names only the parity test, which does skip cleanly. Residual risk, not charged to the child.

Tier evidence is stale for the revised tree: `tier3-evidence.log` omits the P1/P3/P5 executions its contract requires, `tier1-evidence.log` has no clippy/fmt, and `tier2-evidence.log` scopes Python to 13 tests; minimax observes new mtimes but byte-identical content. GLM reports the logs as regenerated and consistent, which minimax's byte-identical observation contradicts. All four lenses reran every probe themselves and all passed, so this is a verifier-process gap, not a DoD failure.
The `implementer-summary.json` test counts are stale (79 in `verification_evidence`, 80 in `dod_probe_notes`, actual 81). Confirmed by all three lenses that checked; no test is missing from the tree.

The Python `pending_requests`/`pending_dropped` maps remain capacity-unbounded on the request path (pre-existing, tightened by the child's unknown-id guard, disclosed accurately in the ADR). All four lenses classify this as residual risk rather than a hard-rule violation because it is lifecycle-scoped, pre-existing, and unreachable as a growth path from the shipped Rust client.

Sidecar adapters use `dropped.store(...)` (overwrite) rather than `fetch_add`, and a late `Done` could land after a failed turn's telemetry drain, misattributing a drop count to the next turn. No test drives the interrupt interleaving.

The two halves of the non-zero sidecar telemetry story are proven separately (real-plugin overflow reaches the adapter; `ReportingStt` double reaches `TurnReport`) but never joined in one test that drives `Session` with a real overflowing `SidecarStt`.

The effective STT window is the last 640 ms (64 frames x 10 ms); longer utterances are transcribed from their tail, and the ADR states the mechanism but not this user-visible consequence. Minimax verified empirically (70 frames in -> 64 retained, dropped=6, retained frames 6..69).

`CancelledTombstones.evicted` is stderr-only and invisible to the runtime's typed telemetry; the client drains the child's stderr into an unbounded `String` at `crates/voicekit-sidecar/src/client.rs:78-87`.

Differential coverage still excludes VAD and timestamp/clock divergence; the parity arms share an in-process `FakeVad` and the projection normalises timestamps. The round-1 STT coverage gap is closed.
`EventQueueStats` collapses `Replaced`, `Dropped` and control refusal into one `dropped` counter, and queue depth is sampled only at turn end (no live per-queue depth/drop time series).

The new 10 ms chunking is not proven to preserve transcript content: the plugin's `FakeStt` ignores PCM, and the trailing partial chunk when the PCM length is not a multiple of `samples_per_frame` is untested explicitly (benign because the plugin concatenates).

`SidecarStt::transcribe` materialises the whole utterance into per-frame `Vec`s before opening the request, so peak memory is ~2x the utterance and the frame vector is bounded only by input length (not a hard-rule violation).
Loss on a failed turn is unobservable: `Session::fail` deliberately drains the adapters but `SessionEvent::Failed` carries no drop counters.

reasons: All four lenses return APPROVE on revision 2. Every DoD probe passes 4/4 with matching evidence: P1 `cargo test --workspace` 81 passed / 0 failed (all four measured 81), P2 exit 0 with fake-only providers and all four counters, P3 27 passed, P4 exit 0 with STT/LLM/TTS all served by the real Python plugin and `sidecar_dropped_frames` distinct, P5 all three grep legs exit 0.

The round-1/2 load-bearing blocker and ADR defects are genuinely closed, and the synthesizer verified the closure in source rather than relying on the reports: `SttProvider` now has a defaulted `take_sidecar_dropped_frames` (`traits.rs:97-104`), `SidecarStt` binds `dropped_frames` on the terminal `Done` (`provider.rs:335`), the session sums stt+llm+tts with `saturating_add` (`session.rs:487-494`), and the ADR now scopes the bound claim to audio/event queues, discloses the lifecycle-scoped plugin maps, and titles point 3 'Loss is observable end to end, on the path that can actually lose' with explicit zero semantics (`docs/adr/0001-architecture.md:50-79`). The new integration test `sidecar_stt_captures_the_plugin_dropped_frames` and unit test `sidecar_dropped_frames_includes_the_stt_adapter` exist.

No lens reports a hard-rule violation; all four mark 'Violated by: none'. `voicekit-core` is undiffed so `TurnState` and the control-event drop rule are unchanged; the default turn spawns no Python (PATH-shim proof); the single monotonic clock is preserved with index-derived STT timestamps; cancel stays idempotent and non-fatal; the protocol change is one additive `#[serde(default)]` JSON field; no forbidden path was edited; and no provider was added (`ReportingStt`/`ReportingTts` are `#[cfg(test)]` doubles).

The remaining modern-technique gaps are advisory or explicitly out of scope: no reference-model property comparison, no mutation-testing evidence, and static (non-adaptive/credit) capacities. None is a blocker under the verdict thresholds, and the ADR documents the out-of-scope deferral.

The tier-evidence artifacts are stale for the revised tree (tier-3 omits P1/P3/P5; tier-1 omits clippy/fmt; tier-2 scopes Python to 13 tests), and GLM's report that they were regenerated is contradicted by minimax's byte-identical-content observation. Per composition rule 1, this is recorded as a residual process-risk item rather than a DoD failure because all four lenses independently reran the probes and all passed.

One cross-lens contradiction surfaced and was resolved by direct inspection, not by vote: minimax cites a persisted `properties.proptest-regressions` seed, while codex found none and kimi says revision 2 deleted it. The current tree contains no such file, so the citation is stale. Because the claim is non-load-bearing (the property passes at 128 and 512 cases), it does not meet the ESCALATE bar of contradictions on >=3 load-bearing claims.

Non-blocking residual risks for the operator: the effective STT window is the last 640 ms, so utterances longer than that are transcribed from their tail (minimax A1); `cargo test --workspace` is not Python-free-safe due to two pre-existing sidecar tests (kimi); and the eviction counter remains stderr-only (codex).
next_action_recommended: APPROVE and ship v0.1 as-is; no blocking changes. Open follow-up tickets (none gate this iteration): (1) regenerate tier-1/2/3 evidence against the final tree so tier-3 actually contains P1/P3/P5; (2) add one end-to-end test driving a real overflowing `SidecarStt` through `Session` and asserting `TurnReport.sidecar_dropped_frames > 0`; (3) state the effective 640 ms STT tail window in the ADR; (4) give `pending_requests` an explicit capacity/counter or keep the lifecycle-scoping disclosure; (5) add mutation-testing or a model-based property to demonstrate the suite kills mutants; (6) extend the differential to VAD/timestamps; and (7) fix the stale test count in `implementer-summary.json`.
